evals.prompt: For a slide in my personal-agents talk I need a diagram comparing the three ways people run personal agents today. Self-hosted (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent): you run the computer (laptop, home server or VPS), any model, memory and credentials on your hardware, security is entirely yours, free software plus model tokens, used by developers and tinkerers. Managed open source (e.g. xCloud): a hosting company runs it on a dedicated server, any model with your own API keys, patching handled but credentials sit with a small host, from $9.99/month, for enthusiasts who don't want to run servers. Productized (Muse, dots, Grok Bot, Gemini Spark): the vendor runs a VM per user, with the vendor's own model, memory and credentials in the vendor's cloud and vault, guard models, approvals and audit trails, free to about $200/month, for mainstream consumers.
